text:
alice: Heads up — since yesterday's merge (PR #4127) we've seen a 20-30% p95 latency spike on streaming responses in prod, mostly for short-turn chat/stream flows. Notable increase in tail. :eyes:
ben: Ugh. Which parts of the change touched runtime? The PR touched SSE framing + tool-calling serialization, right?
alice: Exactly. PR changed SSE chunk flushing to batch writes and switched tool-call args to compact JSON serialization path. Also included a small tweak to kernel selection heuristic (fallthrough for int8 kernels) that got rebased in.
charlie: Do we have a CI perf alert / job that flagged this?
ci-bot: perf-ci/stream-p95 failed on build sha 7b2f1ae — p95 increased from 82ms -> 110ms (34% regression). See: https://ci.internal/perf/7b2f1ae
ben: OK can someone bisect? Quick git bisect across main between last-known-good (sha: e9c4d2a) and the merge commit (sha: 7b2f1ae).
dana: I ran a quick bisect this morning. Bad commit appears to be 3c9a5d1 — the one that changed SSE buffering behavior. Command I used:
```
# bisect
git bisect start 7b2f1ae e9c4d2a
git bisect run ./scripts/run_perf.sh --target stream-p95
```
Results point to 3c9a5d1 (proto: sse:buffer -> batch flush).
emma: Profiling traces from prod sampling show time moved from attention kernels to run_serialize_json in the event loop. Flame: run_event_loop -> serialize_tool_args -> write_sse_batch. CPU time in attention kernel dropped slightly but overall latency higher because we hit more syscalls and more small writes.
charlie: That suggests two effects: (1) SSE batching added internal buffering so first-byte latency waits for flush window, (2) serialization is now on the hot path causing GC/alloc pressure for short responses. Any KV cache anomalies?
alice: We also observed increased KV cache misses for cached prefixes — looks like cache key generation includes a header token that the PR changed ordering of, so cache hit rate dropped ~8% for small prompt prefix cases. That magnifies the problem for short-turn chats.
dana: Reproduced locally with a minimal harness: 10ms write-sse-flush window caused p95 to shift. If I force immediate flush, latencies return to baseline. Patch snippet:```diff
- sse_buffer.append(chunk)
- if batch_window(): flush()
+ sse_buffer.append(chunk)
+ // batch writes to reduce syscalls
+ schedule_flush(batch_window)
```
ben: Given this is a release blocker, propose we revert the SSE batching part of the PR immediately and keep the compact-JSON change behind a feature flag for now. Thoughts? :+1:
charlie: I agree. The kernel-selection tweak likely amplified harm by changing small-batch kernel choice — we should rollback that too or at least pin heuristic to previous behavior until we can evaluate.
emma: I'll open a perf-hotfix PR that reverts the SSE flush scheduling and pins kernel heuristic. Also adding a non-blocking serializer path (offload to background thread) as follow-up.
ops-bot: deploy candidate hotfix (sha: a4f0d5c) to staging started. 0/3 healthy -> 3/3 healthy in 18s.
ci-bot: perf-ci/stream-p95 for hotfix a4f0d5c shows p95 back to 85ms (within noise).
alice: After deploying hotfix to prod (rollout 10%), p95 dropped back to ~88ms and KV cache hit rate recovered as we reverted header reorder. Rolling remainder now. Thanks everyone. :tada:
ben: Postmortem action items?
charlie: Short list: 1) Don't move serialization into event loop without async offload; 2) Add perf unit test for SSE first-byte latency (detect batching regressions); 3) Make kernel-selection changes gated behind perf CI microbenchmarks for small-batch short-seq scenarios; 4) Add KV-cache-key unit tests to catch header-order regressions.
dana: I'll own tests 2+4. Emma will own async serializer prototype.
emma: Yep, will ship a prototype and benchmark.
alice: Filing follow-up tickets and linking PRs in the thread. Thanks for quick triage. :heart:
